items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the unlabelled lemma at source lines 2613-2632, original Lemma 8.9.2, the "Encode-decode for Truncations of Loop Spaces" statement of section 8.9: for a pointed type (A,a0), a fibration code whose fibres are k-types, together with c0, a decoding map and the two round-trip identifications, the k-truncated loop space at a0 is equivalent to code(a0). The author gave it no label, so its first-edition position is part of its identity. The proof (source lines 2634-2645) is a miniature argument of the encode-decode method: the first composite is immediate from the third hypothesis, while the second requires a truncation induction that is only legitimate because paths in a k-type are again a k-type, a path induction inside the truncated family, and a reduction of encode through its recursion rule before the fourth hypothesis applies; none of these steps appears in the statement.
